findings.text: A reset can leave `this.skip` set, and it then swallows later lines. `Store.read()` clears `skip` only when it is called, but `live.js:40` calls `read()` only when the frame has lines (`lines.length && offset > at`). A reset on a file that is now empty or gone gets an empty frame (`ext/JSONL/doc/live.md:66`), so `skip` stays armed. The next ordinary append whose text matches an old line (a bare `{"increment()":{}}`) is consumed and never applied. Fix: clear `skip` on the first frame after the reset even when it is empty (or in `live.js`'s `jsonl()` when `offset` is 0), and add a case to `reset.test.mjs`.

The comment above `changed()` is stale: `core/Item/Store.js` ~line 387 still says `reset()` "forgets what was read so a REWRITTEN file replays clean from line 1". That is the old behaviour. Now it skips the lines it has already applied, so the comment should point at `doc/reset.md`.

`ext/JSONL/doc/live.md:62` still says `jsonl_reset` "arrives only for a file that had already streamed and then shrank". `Tail.js` now also sends it for same-size and longer rewrites and on a resubscribe that fails the gap check. Update that paragraph and link `core/Item/doc/reset.md`.

`core/doc/status.md:14` and `:49` still list "recovery after a file is rewritten (`reset`/`epoch`, gap check)" as not built. Mark it built with a link to `core/Item/doc/reset.md`, and note that `epoch` was skipped on purpose.

`core/Item/doc/reset.md`, "The problem", gives the research link as `research/2026/10/29/persistence-sync/lessons/sync-protocol.md`. The file is at `.../persistence-sync/persistence-sync/lessons/sync-protocol.md`, so the link is broken. It should also be a site link, not bare text.

The snapshot branch (`reset()` sets `this.frozen` and warns once) has no test, though the brief asks for a failing test first for each step. One case in `reset.test.mjs` would pin it: a store with `snapshot` set, reset, read, and the host is unchanged. The decision and its alternative are written down well.

The window proof catches a same-length rewrite only within the 256 bytes before the cursor. `doc/reset.md` "What this does not catch" says so honestly. A real SessionConsolidate url rewrite usually changes length, so the gap check or the shifted window should still catch it. A hash of the whole prefix, or `epoch`, is the upgrade if that case ever shows up.

In `Tail.changed()`, sockets at the same offset share one rewrite check, using the first socket's `proof` (`chunks` is keyed by offset only, `Tail.js` ~line 79). Two sockets can sit at one offset with different proofs (one subscribed before a same-size rewrite, one after). The second socket then gets reset when it didn't need to, or misses a reset, depending on Map order. Keying `chunks` by offset plus proof would close this cheaply.

After a migration that puts another folder's lines in front (Tail test D), the client applies those new lines after the ones it already has, not in file order. For order-sensitive verbs, the recovered host can then differ from a fresh replay. The doc's "identical to a fresh replay" claim is only tested for appended lines.

Requirements check: step 1 is met (shorter, same size, two longer shapes and a rename-over in `Tail.rewrite.test.mjs`). Step 2 is met apart from findings 1 and 6. Step 3 (`epoch` skipped, with the reason in the doc) is met. Step 4 is met: the log has both summary lines, 215 passed with 1 pre-existing timeout (`Files.move.test.mjs`), and ReplayCompare shows 4046 records identical. Step 5 (`doc/reset.md`, linked from `core/Item/readme.md`) is met. `live.js` needed no change. The Store.js edits stay inside `read()`, `reset()` and three new helpers, as the fence allows. A fresh agent could carry on from `session.jsonl`'s log lines and `doc/reset.md`.
